channel.title: AD Biomarker Field Brief
channel.description: A curated evidence monitor for Alzheimer disease biomarkers, clinical trials, clinical guidelines, and management updates that may change scientific exchange, diagnosis, treatment, care, or access.

item.title: CELIA two-year extension strengthens the diranersen signal but remains nonconfirmatory
item.description: At week 96, the 60 mg twice-yearly group had a sponsor-reported 1.09-point CDR-SB advantage versus participants originally assigned placebo, but the comparison extends beyond the randomized placebo-controlled period and follows a failed prespecified dose-response endpoint.

item.title: POLARIS-AD is positive only in the prespecified monotherapy population
item.description: AR1001 missed the 52-week CDR-SB comparison in all 1,535 participants but met the multiplicity-controlled objective in the 604-person subgroup not using symptomatic AD drugs, with a 0.44-point difference.

item.title: HOPE misses its overall endpoint despite a favorable mild-AD subgroup
item.description: The 673-person pivotal trial did not meet its overall primary endpoint; in a prespecified 395-person mild-AD subgroup, the sponsor reported 56% less ADCS-ADL decline and 47% less CDR-SB decline, both nominal findings without published absolute differences.

item.title: Bepranemab misses the phase 2 CDR-SB endpoint
item.description: In 460 treated participants, neither bepranemab dose improved week-80 CDR-SB versus placebo; the 90 mg/kg arm numerically declined more, while safety was broadly similar across groups.

item.title: Amyloid PET reference region changed estimates of treatment response
item.description: Reference-region choice affected apparent longitudinal amyloid change; a favorable exploratory association for white matter did not survive the same-tracer sensitivity analysis.

item.title: Late acquisition dynamics differed across two amyloid PET tracers
item.description: Late tracer kinetics differed, particularly in white matter; small average bias in abbreviated reconstructions does not establish clinical interchangeability.

item.title: Elecsys p-tau217 cutoffs performed similarly to locally derived cutoffs in China
item.description: Existing Elecsys cutoffs performed similarly to locally derived values in this PET-referenced Chinese cohort, with about one in six in the gray zone.

item.title: Plasma biomarker prescreening flagged ineligible participants before START confirmation
item.description: The blood-first workflow identified 12.7% as ineligible at the biomarker stage, but the poster does not establish how many scans it saved.

item.title: Lumipulse blood testing matched CSF accuracy among determinate results
item.description: Plasma p-tau217 had similar accuracy to CSF when it yielded a determinate result, but the plasma gray zone was larger, particularly for the ratio.

item.title: Structured digital APOE disclosure was noninferior to clinician telehealth in eSMARTER
item.description: Structured digital APOE disclosure met noninferiority criteria, but the trial did not establish equivalence for routine portal-only p-tau217 delivery.

item.title: Capillary brain-derived p-tau217 showed potential for remote triage
item.description: The capillary assay discriminated amyloid PET status in a small subset, a route worth studying for triage rather than confirmation.

item.title: Elecsys CSF Aβ42/Aβ40 agreement depended partly on specimen storage
item.description: An automated CSF amyloid ratio agreed well with PET overall; storage and choice of PET reference both affected interpretation.

item.title: Japan approved Lumipulse plasma components for amyloid-pathology assessment
item.description: Japan's two component approvals establish a regulatory route for the automated Lumipulse plasma ratio; reimbursement and ordering are separate.

item.title: A Lumipulse p-tau217 cutoff held up across several memory-clinic cohorts
item.description: The same 0.193 pg/mL cutoff performed well in several specialist cohorts, supporting further assessment of a portable cutoff on this platform, not across assays.

item.title: A plasma eMTBR-tau immunoassay tracked advanced insoluble tau
item.description: An investigational blood immunoassay separated advanced tau stages, but many samples were unquantifiable and it is not a replacement for tau PET.

item.title: Plasma p-tau217 added to estimated absolute risk of cognitive impairment
item.description: Higher Lumipulse p-tau217 shifted modeled 5- and 10-year risks of incident MCI, illustrating a prognostic use distinct from pathology detection.

item.title: eMTBR-tau elevations were not unique to Alzheimer disease
item.description: eMTBR-tau can rise in disorders other than AD, including chronic traumatic encephalopathy, limiting disease-specific interpretation.

item.title: Mayo introduced a new FDA-label PrecivityAD2 send-out order
item.description: The new Mayo order makes the cleared interpretation and specimen workflow explicit; do not carry over the prior single cutpoint.

item.title: Japan added APOE testing considerations to optimal-use guidance for antiamyloid therapy
item.description: The Japanese guidance adds consideration of APOE testing for ARIA risk assessment without replacing surveillance imaging.

item.title: Florbetapir PET software yielded different thresholds, even in Centiloids
item.description: Centiloids improved between-platform agreement over SUVR, but two commercial packages still yielded substantially different cutoffs against the same visual reference.

item.title: CMS finalized separate hospital-outpatient payment status for Tauvid in 2027
item.description: Tauvid remains separately paid under hospital OPPS after temporary pass-through expires, under a different payment classification.

item.title: Adding Aβ42 improved p-tau217 amyloid models, but cutoffs did not travel uniformly
item.description: Adding Aβ42 modestly improved discrimination across three cohorts, with stronger evidence for the model than for universal operating thresholds.

item.title: Similar plasma p-tau217 AUCs masked differences in assay handling
item.description: AUC alone did not distinguish the three p-tau217 workflows: precision and freeze-thaw resilience differed.

item.title: UnitedHealthcare specified ARIA monitoring and IV lecanemab maintenance criteria
item.description: The November policy makes MRI timing and continued every-two-week dosing documentation more explicit without replacing PET or CSF for amyloid confirmation.

item.title: Real-world p-tau217 testing reshapes diagnostic pathways
item.description: Across 1,368 consecutive patients at 24 centers, routine plasma p-tau217 testing produced a 19.9% equivocal zone and was associated with fewer CSF requests and reported reductions in diagnostic delay, but the observational design does not establish patient-outcome benefit.

item.title: Short-interval repeats rarely resolve p-tau217 gray zones
item.description: In 92 paired samples, Lumipulse p-tau217 had ICC 0.94 and within-person CV 11.2%; 8% crossed one probability boundary, and averaging duplicate samples did not reduce the indeterminate group.

item.title: Quantile mapping best mitigates p-tau217 assay effects
item.description: Across 330 participants measured on four p-tau217 platforms per cohort, quantile normalization or mapping most reduced assay effects, while conditional quantile mapping performed best across cohorts; the methods are for research harmonization, not clinical result conversion.

item.title: ALZT-OP1 misses both prespecified phase III comparisons
item.description: In the 594-participant modified intention-to-treat population, cromolyn plus ibuprofen did not improve 72-week CDR-SB versus either component alone; an exploratory APOE4-noncarrier comparison with placebo also missed statistical significance.

item.title: UK consensus guidance restricts blood testing to clinically suspected AD
item.description: ABN and RCPsych guidance recommends plasma p-tau217 as the preferred blood biomarker, testing only after comprehensive assessment and objective cognitive impairment, and a two-cutoff pathway with CSF or PET follow-up for indeterminate results.

item.title: SynVesT-1 PET did not establish noninferiority to FDG PET
item.description: In 94 patients referred for cognitive-decline imaging, quantitative 18F-SynVesT-1 PET had lower AUC than 18F-FDG PET for AD (0.71 vs 0.81), and the prespecified noninferiority margin was not met.
